sentences.text: Avaceratops was a small plant-eating dinosaur belonging to the group of horned dinosaurs known as ceratopsians.
The original specimen, which may have been a young individual, was estimated to be about 2.3 meters long.
Its head features a large bone at the front of the frill with a smooth, curved edge instead of a stepped one.
The name honors Ava Cole, the wife of the fossil finder, and the Lammers family who owned the land.
A larger version of this dinosaur, reaching four meters in length, would have weighed approximately one tonne.
Fossil dealer Eddie Cole first found remains of this animal in 1981 within the Judith River Formation of Montana.
Peter Dodson formally named the species Avaceratops lammersi in 1986 based on these initial finds.
Later, researchers added two earlier skull fragments and described a second, larger skull found in 1999.
As a herbivore, it likely used a sharp beak to bite leaves and needles from ferns, cycads, and conifers.
A 2013 study identified it as the closest relative to the genus Nasutoceratops, forming a group called Nasutoceratopsini.
This dinosaur lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, roughly 80 million years ago.
It inhabited a wet, heavily forested environment in what is now the Northwest United States.
